extraction.name: BoolQ: Exploring the Surprising Difficulty of Natural Yes/No Questions
extraction.description: A reading comprehension dataset of naturally occurring yes/no questions, where each question is paired with a paragraph from a Wikipedia article containing the answer.
extraction.creator: Christopher Clark, Kenton Lee, Ming-Wei Chang, Tom Kwiatkowski, Michael Collins, Kristina Toutanova
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions are gathered from anonymized, aggregated queries to the Google search engine. Queries likely to be yes/no questions are heuristically identified. If a Wikipedia page is returned as one of the first five results, the question and page are given to a human annotator. Annotators label question/article pairs in a three-step process: deciding if the question is good, finding a passage containing the answer, and marking the answer as yes or no. The dataset combines 13k questions from this pipeline with 3k questions from the Natural Questions training set.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Anonymized, aggregated queries to the Google search engine and Wikipedia articles.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions are paired with a specific paragraph from the Wikipedia article instead of the entire document to reduce ambiguity and keep input size manageable.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Queries are filtered to identify those likely to be yes/no questions based on indicator words and length. Only questions where a Wikipedia page is among the first five search results are kept. Questions are filtered to ensure they are comprehensible, unambiguous, and request factual information. Questions marked as 'not answerable' are excluded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human annotators performed a three-step process: 1) Judged if the question was 'good' (comprehensible, unambiguous, factual) before seeing the passage. 2) Found a passage within the document containing enough information to answer the question. 3) Marked the answer as 'yes' or 'no'.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotation quality was assessed by having three authors label 110 randomly chosen examples. The answer annotations reached 90% accuracy compared to gold-standard labels. Disagreements were resolved by mutual agreement. Errors were mostly due to ambiguous/debatable cases or annotator misunderstanding.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to test models on their ability to answer naturally occurring yes/no questions, which are directly related to the practical end-task of answering user yes/no questions. It highlights the difficulty of natural language understanding and inference.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset exhibits class imbalance, with 'yes' answers being slightly more common (62.31% in the train set). There is a correlation between question topic/type and the likelihood of a 'yes' answer, though it is weak. The dataset is derived from Google search queries, which may reflect biases in user search behavior.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset contains naturally occurring questions which may be ambiguous or require complex inference. The 'yes' answer bias exists. The dataset is limited to questions answerable by Wikipedia passages. The analysis of reasoning types may be slightly out-of-date as the dataset has been updated since the analysis was carried out.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. Specifically for reading comprehension, natural language inference, and transfer learning baselines for yes/no question answering.
